sections.title: Recommendation approaches matched to your catalog and users
sections.description: The right algorithm depends on catalog size, interaction data and freshness requirements.

items.title: Content-Based Filtering
items.description: Recommendations from item attributes — ideal for new catalogs or items with little interaction history.

items.title: Collaborative and Hybrid Filtering

items.label: Hybrid

items.title: Embedding-Based Recommendation

blocks.heading: Catalog and interaction scale
paragraphs: Below about 500 items, popularity and editorial curation often outperform machine learning. ML recommendation delivers clear returns at 1,000+ items with meaningful interaction volume, and we tell you honestly which side of that line you are on.

blocks.heading: Seasonality and freshness
paragraphs: We handle seasonality with time-decay weighting, seasonal features and explicit override rules, and set the retraining schedule — daily for high-velocity catalogs, weekly for stable ones — during architecture design.

blocks.heading: Measured with A/B testing
paragraphs: A/B testing design, implementation and statistical analysis are standard deliverables, so the impact of every recommendation change is measured, not assumed.

items.question: How much does a recommendation engine cost?
items.answer: $40,000–$200,000. The most common enterprise deployments — hybrid collaborative and content-based recommendation for eCommerce or media platforms — run $55,000–$120,000.

items.question: What is the minimum catalog size?
items.answer: There is no strict minimum, but below about 500 items simple popularity and editorial curation often outperform ML. ML recommendation delivers clear value at 1,000+ items with substantial user interaction data.

items.question: How often does the model need retraining?
items.answer: It depends on catalog turnover and interaction volume — daily for high-velocity eCommerce, weekly for stable catalogs. We set the schedule during architecture design.

items.question: Can recommendation engines work for B2B?
items.answer: Yes, with adaptations for multiple stakeholders per account, longer purchase cycles and account-level rather than individual-level personalization.

items.question: Do you provide A/B testing to measure impact?
items.answer: Yes. A/B testing design, implementation and statistical analysis are standard deliverables for every recommendation engine we build.

sections.heading: Recommend what each user actually wants next
sections.text: Tell us about your catalog, traffic and where recommendations would appear. An engineer will reply within one business day with an approach and budget range.
